identityReview.decision: Retain common CVE identity explicitly assigned by Next developer API and Librsvg CNA/RustSec. Preserve both wrapper and upstream packages through separate curated overlays; do not drop Librsvg affected ranges when merging.
identityReview.scope: Next developer describes upstream image-optimization memory issue on glibc Linux and workaround sharp>=0.35.5. CNA describes Librsvg nested-XInclude use-after-free. Their assessments and package-specific version ranges are not interchangeable.

caveats: Developer API first pass reached rate limit on 11 public advisories. All 11 public HTML fallbacks returned 200 and were read; first failed attempts remain distinct.
One earlier successful Next.js developer API fetch is also retained in projected fields; its later rate-limit response did not destroy the earlier good response.

Developer structured and Reviewed package fields both say tome, while developer narrative and independently fetched fixed-release repository/npm metadata identify toml; the curated correction and original evidence are recorded in packageIdentityReview. The pypdf 6.2.10 versus narrative/Reviewed 6.21.0 discrepancy, source severity differences and deployment conditions remain attributed.
Full report payloads and PoCs were not executed or published. Review used structured version/date fields and relevant description conditions; it is not independent exploit validation.
curationDecision: sprintf-js remains a database-level withdrawn record: the retrieved public issue comment has author_association NONE and is not claimed as a maintainer source. CNA rejection and Reviewed withdrawal retained in this audit; no fabricated maintainer attribution.
